subject: Deal handoff: ACME - GPU supply assurance and sizing ask
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Rodriguez <emily.rodriguez@acmeretail.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Deal handoff: ACME - GPU supply assurance and sizing ask

Hi Emily, team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward the pilot statement of work, Acme mentioned wanting a guaranteed level of dedicated capacity for the first 90 days of the pilot plus a short burst allowance during holiday peak tests. To get this scoped and priced I need a quick confirmation from Finance and Infra on two fronts so we can finish the mutual action plan: 

1) Sizing: please review the attached worksheet (acme_capacity_request_v2.xlsx) — it has the expected concurrent session profile, target p95 latency, and projected token throughput per hour. We need a recommended reserved slot count and a recommended burst buffer (both in GPU-hours) for Q4 pilot windows.

2) Supply / timeline: can Infra confirm availability for T4/RTX8000-equivalent pools and any lead times for provisioning dedicated pools vs using burst from shared fleet? If there's a capacity risk, propose fallback (model variant, quantization profile) and cost delta.

3) Finance: rough revenue cadence for the pilot (monthly committed $) vs expected overage rates if burst used. We want numbers for a conservative and a bullish scenario.

Emily — if you can share the procurement timeline (PO lead time / SOW sign date target) that helps us map provisioning dates.

Can we get initial numbers by EOD Friday so Sales has a go/no-go for commit wording in the SOW draft?

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: acme_capacity_request_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emily Rodriguez <emily.rodriguez@acmeretail.com>, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal handoff: ACME - GPU supply assurance and sizing ask

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick finance notes:

- We need committed monthly billing vs one-time provisioning fee broken out. For the pilot, do we expect a flat monthly reserved fee or a ramp schedule? The attachment had a few usage patterns; I can model both.
- Please confirm the expected contract start date (effective date) and the pilot length; I’ll produce a conservative ARR projection and a 2-scenario P&L for the SOW.

I’ve attached a starting pricing scenario (acme_pricing_scenario.xlsx) with placeholders for reserved vs burst assumptions. I’ll iterate if Infra supplies capacity constraints.

Ask: Tessa, can you confirm the target effective date and whether Acme expects a cancellation window within the 90-day pilot (e.g., 30 days notice)? That changes our revenue recognition and the financial ask for reserves.

Landing page: I’ll aim to have the two scenarios back by Friday EOD.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: acme_pricing_scenario.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-12T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal handoff: ACME - GPU supply assurance and sizing ask

Tessa / Laura —

Short technical readout from infra:

- GPU types: We have limited T4-equivalent reserved capacity in us-west now; RTX8000-equivalent (high-memory) inventory for Q4 is forecasted but not fully guaranteed. Lead time for dedicated pool build (networking + routing + observability hooks) is ~3-4 weeks once the slot count is finalized.
- Burst alternative: We can provision shared-fleet burst credits to cover short peaks with near-zero lead time but higher per-token cost.
- Suggested conservative plan: reserve 60% of expected steady-state concurrent load as dedicated slots, leave 40% as burst credits for holiday testing windows. This reduces upfront commit and shortens provisioning window.

Risks: supply chain for newer accelerators could shift; if Acme requires specific instance types (very high VRAM) we may need additional procurement lead time.

Next steps: propose a 30-minute triage on Thursday to align sizing numbers. Options: Thu 8:00am PST / Thu 11:00am PST / Fri 9:30am PST.

Attachment: gpu_availability_matrix.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

-Logan
Logan Wright
Director, Infrastructure Capacity | Redwood Inference

From: Emily Rodriguez <emily.rodriguez@acmeretail.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-07-13T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deal handoff: ACME - GPU supply assurance and sizing ask

Tessa / Laura / Logan / Priyom —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. We’re targeting an SOW sign on or before Aug 15 and would like the pilot to start the first week of September (flexible by 1–2 weeks). We prefer the dedicated-pool route for predictability but understand the provisioning constraints. The hybrid reserve + burst approach sounds acceptable.

Attached is the initial SOW draft from procurement (ACME_SOW_draft.docx). Procurement is ok with the 90-day pilot but will want a 30-day cancellation clause; hope that does not block finance.

I can do the Thu 11:00am PST triage. Please send a calendar invite and we’ll bring our DevOps lead.

-Emily
Emily Rodriguez
Sr. Product Manager, Retail AI | Acme Retail
---
Attachment: ACME_SOW_draft.docx (document, 45KB)
